content.summary: The live action is a separately frozen, one-family feasibility run and fits the existing 22-call allowance. Its cap is 18 calls with a 1800-second deadline. C0 and C1 passed; the selected family, source bytes, settings, public input and initial ledger are bound before dispatch.
findings: C1 passed 34 actual Java/reference scenarios and detected four adverse executable mutants. No source-to-rule accuracy was proved.
The full four-method study still needs 288 reserved calls and will not be replaced by this one-method run.
All family-office FAQ answers and qualifiers are provided. No hidden scenario table, reference formula or expected result enters model requests.
Extraction differences and missing referenced legal definitions may keep the result unresolved; safe abstention is recorded rather than treated as interpretation success.
Selection identity was missing from Assurance reuse requests; it is now hashed and the stale-selection regression passes.

Historical call protection now verifies immutable prefixes so later authorized calls can append without changing history or raising the ceiling. Checkpoint tampering, ceiling changes, resets and overspend are rejected.
Five focused continuation/runner regressions pass. No other live run may consume the shared ledger concurrently.
If the engine fails, retain the report and journal, diagnose and use remaining calls only after an explicit successor repair review.
